:::{#sol-matmul-product-of-sums-practice}

All three [matrices](#def-matrix) are $k \times k$,
so @thm-matmul-product-of-sums applies with $m = n = k$,
with $\matr{A}$ in place of its $\matr{C}$ and $\matr{C}$ in place of its $\matr{D}$:

$$
\ba
(\matr{A} + \matr{B})(\matr{A} + \matr{C})
&= \matr{A}\matr{A} + \matr{A}\matr{C} + \matr{B}\matr{A} + \matr{B}\matr{C}.
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-product-of-sums)}
\ea
$$

The third term is $\matr{B}\matr{A}$, with $\matr{B}$ on the left,
because $\matr{B}$ comes from the left factor $\matr{A} + \matr{B}$;
it is in general a different matrix from $\matr{A}\matr{B}$,
as @exm-matmul-product-of-sums shows.

:::
